summary.headline: IBM Confluent Turns Real-Time Data Into Real-Time Action Across Four Industries
summary.challenge: An empty grocery shelf, a late irrigation alert and an outdated AI copilot answer share the same data-layer failure: applications didn't receive the right operational context while there was still time to act. Batch pipelines show what happened but cannot trigger real-time actions as conditions change.
solution: IBM Confluent turns raw events into governed, reusable real-time data products using Apache Kafka for durable event streaming and Apache Flink for continuous event processing
Busie connected 13 PostgreSQL and MongoDB databases through shared Kafka streams, enabling operators to search, quote, price, invoice and notify customers from a consistent view

Focal Systems routes shelf-camera detections, product and inventory events through Kafka topics to MongoDB (low-latency operations) and Snowflake (analytics) without direct source-to-store connections
Apache Flink computes live store-level aggregates from millions of daily shelf images, turning detections into out-of-stock events and planogram-compliance signals for Focal Systems
Airy uses Flink to filter, enrich and prepare streaming data for AI copilots—including Flink SQL for natural language queries and retrieval-augmented generation against live inventory topics
SupPlant decouples its irrigation analytics from WhatsApp delivery using Kafka topics as a durable buffer, absorbing weather-driven spikes to hundreds of thousands of farmers
Stream Governance and Schema Registry enforce data contracts, compatibility and lineage across all four deployments

title: How California DMV reduced legacy modernization timelines by 85% with IBM watsonx.ai
description: The California Department of Motor Vehicles worked with IBM Consulting and IBM watsonx.ai to modernize 6 million lines of legacy COBOL and Assembler code, compressing a 5-year manual effort to 15 months and unlocking the business rules needed to build modern digital services for 33 million Californians.

summary.headline: California DMV Cuts Legacy Modernization Timeline 85% Using IBM watsonx.ai
summary.challenge: The California DMV supports 33 million licensed drivers, nearly 35 million vehicle registrations and collects USD 14 billion in annual revenue. Its core systems—built in the late 1970s across 6 million lines of COBOL and Assembler—still ran critical services, but decades of undocumented modifications by personnel no longer available made it impossible to safely extract the embedded business rules needed to build modern digital experiences.
solution: IBM Consulting, IBM ARC and IBM watsonx.ai designed a structured modernization pipeline for the California DMV
IBM ARC performed static analysis on 2,500 COBOL and Assembler programs—identifying structure, dependencies, variables, conditional logic and business-rule patterns
ARC generated size/complexity metrics, call chains, pseudocode, business-rule summaries, program-to-data dependency reports, structure diagrams and logical flow diagrams
Pseudocode was fed into IBM watsonx.ai, where an LLM converted extracted logic into business-readable English using prompt engineering, tuning and iterative refinement
Outputs were delivered as spreadsheets combining original code snippets, pseudocode and watsonx.ai-generated summaries—giving DMV experts a single review surface
IBM mainframe experts validated syntax accuracy; DMV subject matter experts reviewed outputs for policy and regulatory accuracy
The AI workflow operated entirely from source code with no connection to production systems or live citizen data, eliminating operational risk during analysis
Every generated rule was linked back to the original program and source line for full traceability and auditability
key_outcomes: Legacy modernization timeline reduced by 85%—from an estimated 5 years to 15 months
Nearly 5 million lines of COBOL and Assembler code analyzed in the first year
COBOL extraction accuracy improved from ~30% to 80%
Assembler extraction accuracy improved from 0% to 75%
6 million lines of legacy code across 2,500 programs documented and made traceable
Reusable modernization foundation created for vehicle registration, driver licensing and other critical DMV systems
Foundation enables future automated test generation, impact analysis, user story creation and microservices design
